field_notes.reason: Paper states asset-growth decile cutoffs but does not explicitly state whether ASSETG cutoffs use NYSE-only stocks or all eligible stocks. Full-sample cutoffs are plausible because the paper says all stocks are allocated into deciles, while NYSE breakpoints are explicitly stated only for size-group controls; however, this should be confirmed by Review Gate before original-method codegen.

evidence.location: Table II caption p.1617; Section II.A p.1622
evidence.quote: "formed based on June(t) asset growth decile cutoffs"; "using the 30th and 70th NYSE market equity percentiles"
evidence.interpretation: The first quote supports decile cutoffs for ASSETG; the second quote limits explicit NYSE breakpoint language to size grouping. The exact ASSETG breakpoint universe is therefore unspecified in the paper text.

field_notes.reason: Paper requires nonzero total assets in both years but does not state a general missing-value imputation policy.

evidence.location: Section I Data p.1613; Appendix p.1648
evidence.quote: "a firm must have nonzero total assets in both years t−1 and t−2"
evidence.interpretation: The paper does not state general imputation; this requirement implies dropping observations without usable nonzero assets for ASSETG.

field_notes.reason: Paper reports decile returns and spread comparisons, but does not explicitly define a tradable long-short factor strategy.

current_value.note: Paper reports high-minus-low spread comparisons but does not explicitly define a tradable simple long-short strategy. Direction is inferred for backtesting from the negative high-minus-low spread / high ASSETG -> low returns relation.

candidate_value.note: Paper reports high-minus-low spread comparisons but does not explicitly define a tradable simple long-short strategy. Direction is inferred for backtesting from the negative high-minus-low spread / high ASSETG -> low returns relation.

evidence.location: Section II.A p.1622; Figure 3 caption p.1626
evidence.quote: "The spread is the difference between the returns of the low growth stocks and those of the high growth stocks."
evidence.interpretation: The paper compares low-growth and high-growth portfolios; long-low/short-high is an implementation inference for factor backtesting.
